values.title: Queries
values.summary: Read and write typed data with the generated client: filters, sorting, pagination and mutations.
values.body:
## Reading rows

TypeScript

```
const recent = await db.tasks
  .where({ done: false })
  .orderBy("createdAt", "desc")
  .limit(20)
  .all()
```

### Filters

Pass an object for equality, or use operators like `gt`, `in` and `like` for everything else.

TypeScript

```
import { gt, like } from "tessera"
 
await db.projects.where({ seats: gt(10), name: like("Acme%") }).all()
```

## Pagination

Use cursor pagination for lists that grow. `page()` returns the rows and a `nextCursor` you pass to the next call.

TypeScript

```
const { rows, nextCursor } = await db.tasks.page({ size: 50 })
const next = await db.tasks.page({ size: 50, after: nextCursor })
```

## Writing rows

```
const task = await db.tasks.insert({ title: "Ship docs", projectId })
```

Rules run on every query

Queries from the browser are checked against your row-level rules, so the same code is safe on the client and the server.
